roadmaps.description:
Phase 1 — Foundation (Years 1-2): Complete a Bachelor of Finance (ed001). Learn Financial Modeling (sk001), Advanced Excel (sk002), Accounting Principles (sk004), and basic SQL (sk015). Take online courses in corporate finance and valuation. Acquire internships in corporate finance.

Phase 2 — Early Career (Years 2-4): Join as a Junior/Research Analyst. Build pitchbooks, prepare financial statements, and run DCF/valuation (sk003). Expand Python for Finance (sk012) capabilities and visualization with Tableau/PowerBI (sk014). Start CFA Level I preparation.

Phase 3 — Intermediate (Years 4-7): Move to Senior Analyst; lead forecasting, performance analysis, and portfolio reviews. Add Regulatory Compliance (sk007) knowledge and stakeholder advisory (sk047). Start mentoring juniors; develop domain expertise (e.g., TMT, Healthcare).

Phase 4 — Advanced (Years 7-12): Transition to Portfolio Manager / Senior Financial Analyst. Lead strategic planning, capital allocation decisions, and M&A support (sk005). Consider MBA (ed002) or CFA charter for promotion.

Phase 5 — Leadership / Specialist: Become Head of Research or FP&A Director. Drive investment strategy, manage teams and client relationships, partner with C-suite. Focus on Risk Quantification (sk008) and advanced model governance.

Phase 1 — Foundation (Years 1-2): Obtain a Bachelor of Finance (ed001). Master Financial Modeling (sk001), Valuation (sk003), Advanced Excel (sk002) and Accounting (sk004). Network and secure top-tier internships in investment banking.

Phase 2 — Analyst Associate (Years 2-4): Work on pitch books, perform due diligence and M&A execution (sk005). Hone negotiation and transaction structuring (sk055). Work long deals and learn client management.

Phase 3 — Associate / VP (Years 4-8): Lead deal execution, manage junior team members, own sections of syndication and capital markets work. Add Regulatory Compliance (sk007) and Risk Quantification basics (sk008).

Phase 4 — Senior (Years 8-12): Transition to Director; originate deals, manage key client relationships, and recruit/lead deal teams. Add Business Development (sk048) and client advisory (sk047).

Phase 5 — Managing Director / Executive: Run industry coverage, influence strategy, lead cross-border transactions and sit on investment committees. Focus on governance and enterprise-level risk (sk007).

Phase 1 — Foundation (Years 1-2): Complete Bachelor of Finance (ed001). Learn Investment Planning (sk006), Financial Modeling (sk001) and client communications (sk047). Pursue CFP or local planning licences.

Phase 2 — Early Practice (Years 2-4): Work as junior planner or paraplanner; build financial plans, tax-aware strategies and client reports. Focus on client acquisition techniques (sk048) and compensation/benefits advice (sk058).

Phase 3 — Independent Planner / Senior Advisor (Years 4-8): Grow a client book, specialize (e.g., retirement planning, HNW clients), and manage multi-disciplinary teams (legal/tax). Use advanced modeling (sk001) and portfolio allocation (sk006).

Phase 4 — Practice Owner / Director: Launch an RIA or advisory group; refine service offerings, compliance and CRM systems. Consider team certifications and advanced training.

Phase 5 — Executive / Thought Leadership: Become a recognized advisor, publish thought leadership, and support policy / industry groups. Expand into family office advisory and complex estate design.

Phase 1 — Foundation (Years 1-3): Study finance or risk (ed001/ed008). Learn Risk Quantification (sk008), regulatory frameworks (sk007) and statistical basics (sk009).

Phase 2 — Risk Analyst (Years 2-5): Work in credit/market/operational risk teams, build stress tests and scenario analyses. Become proficient with reporting tools (sk014) and data sources.

Phase 3 — Specialist (Years 5-9): Own risk models, lead remediation programs and integrate risk into capital planning. Gain certifications like FRM/PRM and deepen governance skills.

Phase 4 — Head of Risk / Enterprise Risk: Implement enterprise risk frameworks (sp010), embed risk appetite and present to Boards. Lead regulatory engagements.

Phase 5 — CRO / Executive: Shape enterprise strategy, manage enterprise-wide capital and risk exposures, and champion risk culture and resilience programs.

Phase 1 — Foundation (Years 1-3): Complete BSc Actuarial Science (ed007). Master Probability & Statistics (sk009), Actuarial Modeling (sk010) and programming basics (sk012).

Phase 2 — Exam Track & Internship (Years 2-5): Pass actuarial exams, gain credits via work-based assessments, apply reserving and pricing models. Learn model validation (sk050).

Phase 3 — Qualified Actuary (Years 5-9): Lead pricing, product design and capital modelling. Specialize in pensions or life insurance (sp011) and regulatory reporting.

Phase 4 — Senior Actuary / Consulting: Lead teams, provide advisory to executive clients, and design hedging strategies. Integrate stochastic calculus (sk011) for advanced work.

Phase 5 — Fellowship / Thought Leadership: Achieve Fellowship status, advise boards, publish research and shape industry best practices.

Phase 1 — Foundation (Years 1-3): Obtain MSc Financial Engineering (ed015) or a quantitative degree. Master Python (sk012), Stochastic Calculus (sk011) and Financial Modeling (sk001).

Phase 2 — Quant Developer / Researcher (Years 2-5): Build pricing libraries, backtest strategies and use model validation (sk050). Become familiar with low-latency systems and C++/Python.

Phase 3 — Desk Integration (Years 5-9): Work closely with traders to implement models, perform intraday P&L analysis, and refine hedging strategies (sk005).

Phase 4 — Lead Quant / Head of Model Development: Oversee model risk, mentor quants, and coordinate cross-functional model delivery.

Phase 5 — Chief Quant / Proprietary Trading: Lead quantitative research, set research agendas, and manage significant books. Publish research and collaborate with academic partners.

Phase 1 — Foundation (Years 1-2): Complete Bachelor of Computer Science (ed003). Learn data structures, algorithms and core languages (Python, Java, JS). Gain proficiency in Frontend (sk017) and Backend (sk016).

Phase 2 — Junior Developer (Years 2-4): Build full-stack projects, understand SQL (sk015), API development (sk016) and version control. Participate in code reviews and tests (sk051).

Phase 3 — Mid-Level (Years 4-7): Own end-to-end features, design services (sk018), and optimize performance. Contribute to architecture decisions and mentor juniors.

Phase 4 — Senior / Tech Lead (Years 7-12): Design system architecture for scale, lead cross-functional teams, and coordinate releases. Deepen cloud knowledge (sk019) and observability (sk052).

Phase 5 — Principal / Engineering Manager: Drive technical strategy, build engineering culture, lead hiring and roadmap prioritization. Option to become an engineering manager or principal engineer.

Phase 1 — Foundation (Years 1-2): Complete a quantitative degree or Bachelor of Computer Science (ed003). Learn SQL (sk015), Python for analysis (sk012) and Data Visualization (sk014).

Phase 2 — Analyst (Years 2-4): Work on data pipelines, ETL, A/B testing and reporting. Own dashboarding and KPI definitions. Learn basic ML (sk013).

Phase 3 — Senior Analyst (Years 4-7): Lead analytics projects, translate business problems into data requirements, and coach junior analysts. Implement scalable data models and warehouses (sk019).

Phase 4 — Analytics Lead / Product Data Scientist (Years 7-12): Set analytics strategy, partner with product and engineering. Use machine learning for predictive analytics and decisioning.

Phase 5 — Head of Data / Analytics Director: Oversee analytics teams, implement data governance, and tie analytics to business outcomes and ROI.

Phase 1 — Foundation (Years 1-2): Complete MSc Machine Learning (ed010) or a strong CS degree. Master Python (sk012), ML frameworks and statistics (sk009).

Phase 2 — ML Engineer (Years 2-4): Build models, productionize with MLOps techniques (sk020, sk021), and learn deployment patterns and observability (sk052).

Phase 3 — Specialization (Years 4-8): Choose domain (NLP, CV — sp013). Optimize models, address bias and governance (sk049), and implement model validation (sk050).

Phase 4 — Senior ML Engineer / Lead (Years 8-12): Own ML platform architecture, CI/CD for models, and cross-team productization. Mentor teams and conduct research collaborations.

Phase 5 — Director of AI / Research Lead: Set AI strategy, manage data and compute resources, and implement responsible AI governance across the organization.

Phase 1 — Cloud Foundation (Years 1-2): Complete BSc Cloud Computing (ed009). Learn Cloud Architecture (sk019), networking basics (sk025) and scripting (sk054).

Phase 2 — Cloud Engineer (Years 2-4): Implement IaC, manage cloud resources and design resilient architectures (sk019, sk020). Work on cost optimisation and security basics (sk022).

Phase 3 — Cloud Architect (Years 4-8): Design large-scale platforms, multi-cloud patterns, disaster recovery and observability (sk052). Obtain vendor certs (AWS/Azure/GCP).

Phase 4 — Cloud Security & Governance (Years 8-12): Specialize in cloud security architecture (sp012), compliance and incident planning (sk024).

Phase 5 — Enterprise Cloud Strategy: Lead Cloud Center of Excellence, drive organisational cloud adoption, and set multi-year migration roadmaps.

Phase 1 — Systems Foundation (Years 1-2): Complete BSc Cloud/DevOps (ed009) or CS degree. Learn Linux, scripting (sk054), CI/CD (sk020) and containerization (sk021).

Phase 2 — DevOps Engineer (Years 2-5): Build pipelines, IaC and automated testing. Implement monitoring and observability (sk052). Work with Kubernetes (sp019).

Phase 3 — SRE / Platform Engineer (Years 5-9): Improve reliability, runbook design, and incident management. Focus on automation and scaling patterns.

Phase 4 — Platform Lead (Years 9-12): Lead platform teams, own developer experience and observability strategy. Drive cross-team improvements and cost optimization.

Phase 5 — Director of Platform / CTO Track: Oversee engineering platform, SRE culture, and infrastructure strategy across products.

Phase 1 — Foundation (Years 1-2): Obtain Bachelor of Computer Science (ed003). Learn Cybersecurity fundamentals (sk022), networking (sk025) and scripting (sk054).

Phase 2 — Defensive Security (Years 2-5): Work in SOC, SIEM tools and threat intelligence. Build incident response skills (sk024) and run tabletop exercises.

Phase 3 — Offensive & Specialization (Years 5-9): Move into penetration testing, forensics (sk023, sk024), or cloud security (sk022). Obtain certifications (OSCP, CISSP).

Phase 4 — Security Architect / Manager (Years 9-12): Develop enterprise security architecture, secure SDLC and risk assessments. Lead response teams.

Phase 5 — CISO / Security Executive: Drive security strategy, compliance and liaison with executive stakeholders. Influence culture and security investment decisions.

Phase 1 — Foundation (Years 1-3): Complete Bachelor of Engineering (ed004). Core courses in dynamics, materials and CAD (sk026).

Phase 2 — Junior Design Engineer (Years 2-4): Produce detailed designs, perform tests and contribute to prototyping. Work on machining, BOMs and supplier engagement.

Phase 3 — Mid-Level / Specialist (Years 4-8): Own system-level designs, apply materials science (sk027) and control systems (sk028). Use Lean & Six Sigma (sk032) for process improvements.

Phase 4 — Senior / R&D Lead (Years 8-12): Lead product groups, manage cross-discipline engineering, and drive prototyping and regulatory compliance (sk056).

Phase 5 — Engineering Director / CTO of Product: Oversee product roadmaps, capital planning, and strategic technical decisions. Option to specialize in robotics (sp005).

Phase 1 — Foundation (Years 1-3): Study civil engineering (ed004). Master structural analysis (sk030), hydrology (sk029) and CAD (sk026).

Phase 4 — Senior / Chartered Engineer (Years 9-12): Obtain professional licensure, lead complex infrastructure projects and manage client relationships. Use Lean & Six Sigma (sk032) for delivery.

Phase 1 — Foundation (Years 1-3): Complete Bachelor of Engineering (ed004) with power electronics and embedded systems. Learn control systems (sk028) and CAD (sk026).

Phase 4 — Senior Engineer (Years 9-12): Lead multidisciplinary teams for generation and distribution projects. Drive technical standards and performance metrics.

Phase 5 — Principal Engineer / Technical Director: Lead national-scale power projects, advise on energy strategy and integration of renewable energy technologies.

Phase 1 — Foundation (Years 1-3): Complete BEng Environmental Engineering (ed012). Study hydrology (sk029), EIAs (sk034) and renewable basics (sk035).

Phase 2 — Field Work & Compliance (Years 2-5): Conduct site assessments, prepare EIA reports, and engage regulators. Build project management (sk031) experience.

Phase 3 — Design Specialist (Years 5-9): Design water systems, remediation solutions and sustainable infrastructure. Apply modelling tools and lifecycle analysis.

Phase 4 — Senior Consultant / Project Lead (Years 9-12): Lead multidisciplinary teams on large sustainability projects, manage budgets and stakeholders.

Phase 5 — Policy / Director Level: Influence regional environmental policy, lead sustainability programs and advise government or large corporates on resilience.

Phase 1 — Foundation (Years 1-3): Obtain BSc Biomedical Engineering (ed016). Learn medical device design (sk036), biomechanics (sk037) and CAD (sk026).

Phase 3 — Clinical Integration (Years 5-9): Work with clinicians in trials, ensure device usability and clinical data collection. Master GCP basics (sk043) for trials.

Phase 1 — Education & Rotations (Years 1-4): Complete Bachelor of Nursing (ed005). Master Clinical Care (sk038), Patient Communication (sk039) and pharmacology basics (sk041).

Phase 2 — Licensure & Competency (Years 2-5): Pass national exams, gain experience in med-surg units, and acquire ACLS/ALS certifications (sk040). Build EMR proficiency (sk053).

Phase 3 — Specialty Exposure (Years 5-9): Rotate through specialties (ICU, ER, Pediatrics) and pursue professional certificates. Start clinical teaching basics (sk042).

Phase 4 — Clinical Lead / Charge Nurse (Years 9-12): Lead shifts, manage staffing and quality improvement (sk057). Mentor new grads and coordinate multidisciplinary care.

Phase 5 — Advanced Practice / Education: Consider NP training (ed006) or transition to education (c022) or nurse management roles.

Phase 1 — Experience Base (Years 1-5): Complete Bachelor of Nursing (ed005) and practice as an RN. Build strong assessment skills (sk038) and complete critical care rotations.

Phase 2 — Advanced Education (Years 3-6): Enroll in Master of Nursing Practice (ed006). Master Advanced Life Support (sk040), Pharmacology (sk041) and Epidemiology basics (sk045).

Phase 3 — Certification & Autonomy (Years 6-10): Obtain NP certification, begin autonomous practice, prescribing and panel management. Enhance clinical teaching (sk042).

Phase 4 — Practice Leadership & Specialization (Years 10-15): Focus on a niche (pediatrics, family medicine — sp008), lead clinics and supervise students.

Phase 5 — Executive / Clinical Director: Lead clinical programs, design care pathways and influence healthcare delivery strategy.

Phase 1 — RN Base (Years 1-3): Complete Bachelor of Nursing (ed005) and acquire initial bedside experience. Take basic critical care courses and ACLS (sk040).

Phase 2 — Advanced Training (Years 2-5): Enroll in Postgraduate Diploma: Critical Care Nursing (ed013). Master haemodynamic monitoring and ventilator management. Strengthen clinical documentation (sk053).

Phase 3 — Sub-Specialization (Years 5-9): Work in ICU, trauma or cardiac units and gain advanced certifications. Lead code teams and simulations.

Phase 4 — Clinical Expert (Years 9-12): Become Clinical Nurse Specialist or unit lead, drive protocols and evidence-based change (sk057).

Phase 5 — Education / Policy Influence: Move into training, OR lead critical care service development and policy for ICU standards.

Phase 1 — Clinical Base (Years 1-4): Gain RN experience (ed005), deliver bedside teaching and master clinical assessment (sk038). Begin pedagogic studies.

Phase 2 — Formal Education Training (Years 3-6): Obtain MEd / Postgrad Diploma in Nursing Education (ed014). Learn curriculum design and assessment (sk042).

Phase 3 — Lecturer / Clinical Educator (Years 5-9): Teach in academic or hospital settings, run OSCEs and develop simulation scenarios (sp017).

Phase 4 — Program Director (Years 9-13): Manage curricula, accreditation and faculty development. Drive simulation-based education and interprofessional learning.

Phase 5 — Dean / Academic Leader: Oversee schools of nursing, research agendas and national training standards.

Phase 1 — Pre-Clinical Training (Years 1-2): Obtain Diploma in Clinical Research (ed017) or life sciences degree. Learn GCP (sk043), epidemiology (sk045) and trial terminology.

Phase 2 — Coordinator (Years 2-5): Run site-level trials: patient recruitment (sk046), informed consent and source data verification. Use data visualization (sk014) for site metrics.

Phase 3 — Senior Coordinator / Manager (Years 5-9): Oversee multiple sites, manage budgets, liaise with sponsors and CROs. Master protocol development (sk044) and regulatory submissions.

Phase 4 — Clinical Trial Manager (Years 9-12): Lead global trial operations, vendor management and complex therapeutic area coordination (sp021).

Phase 5 — Head of Clinical Operations / Director: Run clinical programs, strategic pipeline planning and vendor partnerships. Lead regulatory interactions and product lifecycle planning.

Phase 1 — RN Foundation (Years 1-3): Complete Bachelor of Nursing (ed005). Develop community health basics, epidemiology (sk045) and patient communication (sk039).

Phase 2 — Field Practice (Years 2-5): Work in community clinics, design outreach / screening programs and run health promotion activities. Use data visualization for population health (sk014).

Phase 3 — Program Development (Years 5-9): Design and evaluate public health programs, secure funding and manage stakeholders. Focus on policy, monitoring & evaluation.

Phase 4 — Leadership (Years 9-12): Lead regional public health initiatives, coordinate emergency response and manage multi-disciplinary teams.

Phase 5 — Public Health Director / Policy Advisor: Shape preventive health programmes, contribute to public health strategy, and advise government or NGOs on population-level interventions.
